body_es:
HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) es un protocolo sin estado para transferir documentos web. Usa puerto 80. Los métodos principales son GET (solicitar), POST (enviar datos), PUT (reemplazar), DELETE (eliminar), PATCH (actualizar parcialmente). Los códigos 2xx indican éxito (200 OK, 201 Created), 3xx redirección (301, 302), 4xx error cliente (400, 401, 403, 404), 5xx error servidor (500). HTTPS añade TLS/SSL sobre HTTP para cifrar la comunicación e autenticar el servidor. Usa puerto 443. Los encabezados HTTP incluyen Content-Type, Authorization, Cache-Control. HTTP/1.1 usa conexiones persistentes, HTTP/2 permite multiplexación.

HTTP/1.1 añadió conexiones persistentes (keep-alive) y pipelining. HTTP/2 introduce multiplexing: múltiples solicitudes/respuestas en paralelo sobre una sola conexión TCP, compresión de cabeceras (HPACK) y server push. HTTP/3 usa QUIC sobre UDP. Los métodos HTTP tienen semántica: GET (idempotente, cacheable), POST (no idempotente), PUT (reemplaza recurso completo), PATCH (modifica parcialmente), DELETE, HEAD (como GET sin body), OPTIONS (capacidades del servidor). Cabeceras importantes: `Content-Type` (MIME type), `Authorization` (Bearer token, Basic), `Cache-Control` (max-age, no-store), `CORS` headers para peticiones cross-origin. HTTPS añade TLS: el handshake TLS 1.3 tarda solo 1-RTT. El certificado verifica la identidad del servidor; HSTS obliga al navegador a usar siempre HTTPS. Códigos de estado: 2xx éxito, 3xx redirección, 4xx error del cliente (401 no autenticado, 403 prohibido, 404 no encontrado, 429 demasiadas peticiones), 5xx error del servidor.
body_en:
HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol) is a stateless protocol for transferring web documents. Uses port 80. Main methods are GET (request), POST (send data), PUT (replace), DELETE (remove), PATCH (partial update). Codes 2xx indicate success (200 OK, 201 Created), 3xx redirect (301, 302), 4xx client error (400, 401, 403, 404), 5xx server error (500). HTTPS adds TLS/SSL over HTTP to encrypt communication and authenticate the server. Uses port 443. HTTP headers include Content-Type, Authorization, Cache-Control. HTTP/1.1 uses persistent connections, HTTP/2 allows multiplexing.

HTTP/1.1 added persistent connections (keep-alive) and pipelining. HTTP/2 introduces multiplexing: multiple requests/responses in parallel over a single TCP connection, header compression (HPACK), and server push. HTTP/3 uses QUIC over UDP. HTTP methods have semantics: GET (idempotent, cacheable), POST (not idempotent), PUT (replaces full resource), PATCH (partial modification), DELETE, HEAD (like GET without body), OPTIONS (server capabilities). Important headers: `Content-Type` (MIME type), `Authorization` (Bearer token, Basic), `Cache-Control` (max-age, no-store), `CORS` headers for cross-origin requests. HTTPS adds TLS: the TLS 1.3 handshake takes only 1-RTT. The certificate verifies the server's identity; HSTS forces the browser to always use HTTPS. Status codes: 2xx success, 3xx redirect, 4xx client error (401 unauthenticated, 403 forbidden, 404 not found, 429 too many requests), 5xx server error.
